questions.q: What is a pull request, according to this lesson?
options: A way to permanently delete a branch
A request to merge one branch into another, opened before the merge, with discussion and CI results attached
A command that immediately merges two branches with no review step
A type of commit message format
questions.explain: A PR is GitHub's layer on top of git merge — it's opened before the merge happens, with a place for comments, suggestions, and CI results.

questions.q: What does GitHub typically offer right after you push a new branch?
options: Nothing — you must always open a PR through a separate menu
A yellow banner with a 'Compare & pull request' button
A prompt to delete the branch
An automatic merge into main with no review
questions.explain: GitHub notices the recent push and shows a banner offering to open a pull request directly, without hunting through menus.

questions.q: What two branches does opening a pull request require you to specify?
options: Only the branch you're merging into — GitHub picks the other automatically
The branch with your new commits, and the branch you want them merged into (almost always main)
The remote name and the commit hash
Two completely unrelated repositories
questions.explain: A PR compares two branches: the one with new commits (the head/compare branch) and the one being merged into (the base branch, usually main).

questions.q: According to this lesson, why are pull requests worth using even on a solo project?
options: They replace the need for commits entirely
They are not worth using solo — PRs only matter with a team
A PR is a checkpoint CI runs against before main is touched, and a permanent, searchable record of what changed and why
They automatically fix any bugs in the code
questions.explain: Even alone, a PR gives you a CI checkpoint before main is affected, and a permanent record you can search later.

questions.q: What does a plain 'git merge' skip that a pull request provides?
options: A commit hash
The ability to combine two branches at all
A CI checkpoint and a permanent, searchable record of the change
The staging area
questions.explain: git merge runs locally and instantly with no review step — it skips both the CI checkpoint and the permanent discussion record a PR provides.
